# Shared LLM Wiki web program

This GPL-3.0-only web program adapts `nashsu/llm_wiki@0.6.13`, revision `e08cfce65aad8b76b13546a081c1a8d4422b70c3`.
`WikiNetwork.tsx` adapts the upstream `src/components/graph/graph-view.tsx` graph loading, degree-based sizing, type/community coloring, neighbour highlighting and Sigma controls. Upstream authors retain their copyright. See the component-level LICENSE and provenance records.
The complete pinned graph-view source is retained once in `../upstream/components/graph-view.tsx`; `ADAPTATIONS.json` records its SHA-256, modification date, and the local files and changes derived from it.

The program is built once into `lib/llm-wiki/web.html`, including all JavaScript and CSS. The plugin serves that same file to every authorized knowledge space. No per-employee program, node_modules, desktop backend, Tauri invocation, file path access, model credential, or write endpoint exists in the frame. The right pane renders sanitized, read-only Markdown.

The canvas accepts `graph.kind: "semantic"` and draws only concept/entity pages with evidence-backed semantic relationships. Both Sigma and its SVG fallback apply this boundary independently of the reading directory. Ordinary page links, shared source citations, article membership and overview navigation never become canvas edges. Type legends include only concepts and entities; degree, layouts and communities come from this semantic graph. Statistics count concepts, entities and every directional predicate, including multiple predicates between the same two nodes.

All authorized pages remain in the independent `pages` reading index. The toolbar has no `文章` control. The read-only directory groups B knowledge articles, C overview navigation, concepts/entities and source texts when it opens automatically for a snapshot with articles but no semantic nodes. Concept clicks still open definitions, related B articles and exact A evidence in the right pane. A snapshot with articles but no extracted concepts displays `暂无概念图谱` and automatically opens its read-only directory on space/version binding; its close control still closes the reader. Edge readers show every `source → predicate → target` statement with its explicit/inferred basis and exact citation. This stricter canvas is the integration's product choice, not an upstream rule that all Wiki graphs must exclude source or article pages.

The default overview lays out the complete evidence-bearing semantic network once in deterministic concentric rings. More-connected nodes occupy inner rings, and nodes are evenly spaced around each ring; this replaces the inherited force layout without changing topology. It does not draw component boxes or duplicate group captions; community colors and the legend remain. Disconnected components and isolated nodes do not gain invented bridges. Clicking a concept or entity highlights its true one-hop context and opens the right reader. The canvas has no upper-left relationship list; its directional source/predicate/target statements and expandable evidence live in that reader and remain available while reading a related article or source. Expand relationships first fits that visible neighborhood, then adds one real frontier layer per action; the background network stays available and dimmed. Expansion is local display state bound to the space, snapshot version and root, with no model request or write API.

Reader navigation to supporting articles or exact sources, color changes and locale updates preserve the exploration. A different root, space/version, query or type filter resets it. Hidden bridges cannot reveal cached nodes beyond the visibility boundary. Back to full graph clears reading and filters and restores the overview camera. Sigma and SVG share the same focus set and real induced edges; fitting uses current dragged coordinates and never creates a second graph.

## JSON message protocol, version 1

Every message contains `namespace: "workforce-llm-wiki"`, `protocolVersion: 1`, and `type`.
The frame has `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and an opaque origin. Both parties bind `event.source` to the expected window; the parent also checks `event.origin === "null"`. `postMessage` uses `"*"` because the recipient is sandboxed. The random `channel` is capability material for this single frame instance, never a URL parameter.

1. Frame → parent: `ready`. This only requests initialization and never authorizes data access.
2. Parent → frame: `init { channel, epoch, view, theme, locale?, rebuilding, canRebuild }`. `view` is `WikiLibraryView` containing only the already-authorized knowledge space and the `semantic` graph discriminator. Canvas nodes must match concept/entity reading pages; each retained edge must contain valid, evidence-bearing semantic relations between its endpoints. The frame accepts the first channel from its parent. Subsequent updates must use that channel.
3. Parent → frame: `update` with the same fields. A change to `spaceId` or snapshot `version` increments `epoch`; old selection, preview, requests and graph positions are discarded. Status, theme and locale updates within the same epoch preserve graph and reading state. Optional `locale` accepts only `zh` or `en`; omission defaults to Chinese for older integrations. The parent supplies the current DSH language, and changing it updates controls and accessible names live without rebuilding knowledge. No browser language, frame setting or persistent language preference is consulted. User titles, concepts, predicates, article bodies, source names/text and stored folder names remain verbatim.
4. Frame → parent: `ack { channel, epoch, spaceId, version }`.
5. Frame → parent: `source-request { channel, epoch, spaceId, version, requestId, citation }`. The parent checks all binding fields and matches the exact citation against the current view's pages/semantic edges. The source ID must still be active in this knowledge space. It returns an exact source ID/version from the already-authorized source list when available. When an active source has a newer version while the visible published snapshot still cites the earlier version, the parent uses the existing `knowledgeSource(target, sourceId, version)` capability. The host validates that the exact historical version is cited by the visible snapshot; no arbitrary filesystem path or generic read RPC is accepted.
6. Parent → frame: `source-response { channel, epoch, spaceId, version, requestId, citation, source?: { id, version, title, text }, error? }`. After every asynchronous historical read the parent rechecks the original context, random channel, epoch, space ID, snapshot version, exact citation authorization, and active source ID. A switch, deletion, or stale binding discards the response. The frame renders the cited historical line range and original text in its right pane; it never substitutes the latest source version for an older citation.
7. Frame → parent: `rebuild-request { channel, epoch, spaceId, version }`, only acted on when the parent currently offers rebuilding. This invokes the existing plugin compilation action; there is no generic RPC.

No page click needs a new host request: pages and internal links are scoped to the current authorized view. Untrusted Markdown cannot execute scripts, load images or arbitrary frames, or read the host. External links have no browser navigation capability in the sandbox.

## Accessibility and inspection

The network region is named `知识网络`; canvas rendering has equivalent keyboard-accessible concept/entity buttons. The removed article toolbar control is not replaced elsewhere. An empty semantic graph with existing articles automatically opens the directory, while ordinary graph reading starts from concept/entity nodes. Search, `节点类别`/`知识分组` coloring, `展开关联`/`返回全图`, zoom and fit controls have accessible names. Right readers are named `知识文章阅读`, `知识关系阅读` and `原始资料阅读`. The network exposes its camera and node coordinates as read-only DOM attributes for functional browser regression checks; these are not a browser RPC.


## 0.26.0 compact toolbar

Color mode buttons follow the Knowledge graph title. The separate Back to full graph toolbar button is removed; Fit graph clears filters, exploration and reading selection while fitting the complete graph. This changes UI state only and does not compile or mutate knowledge. The project embedding uses the available panel area without a second frame or version status row.
